topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

outline.topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: Prerequisite: Average Speed vs. Instantaneous Speed
sections.content: Define average rate of change as the slope of a secant line between two points. Use a visual of a Cheetah running to explain that speed varies over time, leading to the need for a more precise measurement at a single moment.
sections.example: A Cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds; its average speed is 20 m/s, but its speedometer fluctuated during the sprint.

sections.title: Visualizing the Limit Process
sections.content: Introduce the 'Zoom-in' effect. Show the secant line between two points on a curve. Gradually bring the two points closer together (Δx → 0). Visually transform the secant line into a tangent line.
sections.example: An animation showing two points on a parabolic path (f(x)=x²) getting infinitely close until the secant line snaps into the tangent line at a specific point.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
sections.content: Formally define the derivative as the limit of the difference quotient: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Connect this directly to the slope of the tangent line at point x.
sections.example: Algebraic derivation for f(x) = x², showing the resulting slope formula is 2x.

sections.title: Application: The Instantaneous Velocity
sections.content: Apply the concept to motion. If position is s(t), the derivative s'(t) gives the instantaneous velocity. This demonstrates the practical utility of derivatives in physics.
sections.example: A drone taking off; use the derivative of its height function to calculate its exact velocity at the 2-second mark.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap that the derivative is simply the 'slope function.' Emphasize that it captures 'instantaneous change' by taking the limit as the interval of change shrinks to zero.
sections.example: A final infographic showing: Secant (Average) -> Tangent (Instantaneous) -> Derivative.
